items.body: After a fallow year and seventeen summers at Charlton Park, WOMAD moves to Neston Park near Corsham in north Wiltshire, running Thursday 23 to Sunday 26 July. Three miles up the road, Peter Gabriel built Real World Studios into an eighteenth-century watermill on the By Brook in 1987, and WOMAD’s own offices have been based there. The festival grew out of what Gabriel was doing at Real World, pulling musicians from across the world into the same building to record together. Forty-four years and two permanent homes later — Reading from 1990 to 2006 and Charlton Park from 2007 to 2024 — the new chapter has clearly landed well with the audience: Tier 1 weekend tickets sold out in under an hour when sales opened. This year’s programme cements some of the strongest partnerships the festival has built in recent years. NTS Radio, the London-based independent broadcaster that has spent fifteen years building a global network of DJs and selectors across more than forty cities, runs a dedicated after-dark stage across all four nights. Bristol’s Saffron, the non-profit that has spent a decade building pathways for women, non-binary and trans artists into music technology and production, takes over one strand of the programme, as does Jam Jar, the independent venue in St Judes that has become one of the city’s most reliable homes for global sounds. Twende, a grassroots collective whose nights pull together selectors from across the Bristol diaspora, and VP Productions, who bring two decades of carnival and Afro-Caribbean club culture, complete the picture. To open its 2026 edition, WOMAD hands Thursday night to Afro-fusionist limewire K.O.G. Kweku Sackey moved from Accra to Sheffield to study in 2008 and built the Zongo Brigade around him, an eight-piece that pulls highlife, hip-hop and soukous together, with Sackey rapping across English, Pidgin and Ga. He also fronts Onipa alongside Tom Excell of Nubiyan Twist, the Afro-futurist project that put out Off The Grid on Strut in 2024. His 2022 album Zone 6, Agege, named after the coastal suburb of Accra where he grew up, and its 2024 follow-up Don’t Take My Soul, both produced by Guts and Excell, draw on his Ghanaian roots and the women who raised him; last year he featured on Africa Express‘ Bahidorá, recorded in Mexico with Damon Albarn and Fatoumata Diawara among thirty-plus collaborators.  Tian Qiyi, playing the same night, are brothers John and Charlie Wardle, who grew up inside the Pagoda Chinese Youth Orchestra in Liverpool, founded by their maternal grandfather and now run by their mother Zi Lan Liao. On their 2025 album Songs For Workers, they set the yangqin (a hammered dulcimer), the erhu (a two-stringed fiddle) and Mongolian strings against the dub bass and post-punk their father Jah Wobble built his name on. After dark the NTS stage opens, running Italo disco and synth-pop into UK bhangra, Desi folk and deep dubby techno across three sets. Greentea Peng headlines the Friday. Born Aria Wells in South London, she calls what she does psychedelic R&B, and it comes out as neo-soul run through dub: heavy on bass, loose in the pocket, her voice moving somewhere between speech and song. Live she works with the Seng Seng Family, a band big enough to stretch songs from her latest album Tell Dem It’s Sunny well past their recorded length. Barrington Levy brings the other end of the reggae lineage. He cut “Here I Come” and “Under Me Sensi” before he was twenty-five, records still pointed to as the foundations of digital dancehall, and forty-odd years on the voice remains the draw, that high, cracked delivery he can still hold a field with.  Mádé Kuti arrives with the weight of the family name and enough of his own to carry it. He played every instrument on his 2021 debut For(e)ward and returned last year with Where Does Happiness Come From?, taking the afrobeat his father Femi and grandfather Fela built somewhere quieter and more searching, less confrontation, more doubt. Wesli draws on that same afrobeat and pushes it further out. Born Wesley Louissaint in Port-au-Prince, he built his first guitar at eight from an oil can and nylon fishing line, and now leads a Montreal band folding Haitian Vodou chant and carnival rara into afrobeat, reggae and hip-hop; his Rapadou Kreyol took the Juno for World Music Album of the Year in 2019, and his latest, Makaya, is named for the mountains that hid the maroons who won Haiti its independence, turns that history of resistance into dance music. Four of Friday’s other sets come from women rebuilding the music they were raised on. Derya Yıldırım plays the bağlama, the long-necked Anatolian lute, and fronts the Berlin band Grup Şimşek; on 2025’s Yarın Yoksa she rebuilds songs she learned from her grandmother around fuzz organ and slow psych drums. ganavya, born in New York, raised in Tamil Nadu, learned the jal tarang and Carnatic singing from her grandmother before Berklee and jazz found her. Her 2025 album Nilam, co-produced by Nils Frahm at his Berlin studio, moves between Tamil, English and Old Marathi over harp, double bass and the yāzh, a bird-shaped Tamil harp reconstructed for the record.    Bogotá trio La Perla play the gaita flutes and Afro-Colombian drums that custom usually reserves for men, three voices over hand percussion, and they play and sing it loud. Annie & the Caldwells are a family from West Point, Mississippi. Annie sings, her husband Willie Joe plays guitar, their sons hold the rhythm section, their daughters and goddaughter sing behind her. They work day jobs and play weekends, and their debut Can’t Lose My (Soul), produced by Sinkane, arrived on Luaka Bop last year, forty years into their life as a band. It is gospel that works a dancefloor. Hip-hop turns up twice on the day, in two very different registers. Birmingham rapper Kofi Stone writes narrative-driven, jazz-inflected hip-hop about faith, family and grief across a trilogy: his 2019 debut Nobody Cares Till Everybody Does, 2024’s A Man After God’s Own Heart, which carried verses from the late Benjamin Zephaniah, and last November’s All The Flowers Have Bloomed, which closed it. Tamer Nafar founded DAM in Lyd in 2000, the first Palestinian hip-hop group, and their ‘Min Irhabi’ (Who’s the Terrorist) passed a million downloads at a time when almost nobody in the Middle East was rapping in Arabic. He performs under his own name, touring January’s In the Name of the Father, the Imam & John Lennon, the first solo record after twenty-five years fronting DAM. The title tracks the two things his father played on car journeys through Palestine, Qur’an recitations and Beatles records, and the album turns that into an imagined conversation with him. Elsewhere it takes on the crime and structural abandonment inside Palestinian communities in Israel, reaches into Gaza through a verse the seventeen-year-old MC Abdul recorded remotely, and folds a traditional Palestinian children’s lullaby into a track built on Detroit techno. Elsewhere on the Friday, Bristol’s Ishmael Ensemble bring the Rituals Orchestra with them, saxophonist Pete Cunningham’s group folding astral jazz into twenty years of the city’s club music, and expanding the five-piece with a string quartet, harp and guest vocalists to reinterpret the 2024 album Rituals. While, after dark, VHOOR takes the NTS stage, Victor Hugo Rodrigues from Belo Horizonte, one of the producers who took chill baile out of SoundCloud and pushed baile funk somewhere between Miami bass, freestyle and afro-house. He is followed by Coco María, Ana Lucia from Saltillo in northern Mexico, now based in Amsterdam, who runs the fortnightly Club Coco show on NTS and digs cumbia, charanga and Latin funk out of Colombia, Mexico, Peru and wherever else the record shops take her. Saturday is built around instruments with histories as articulate as the hands that play them. The ardin, the harp the Moorish griot tradition reserves for women, sits at the centre of everything Noura Mint Seymali does, her husband Jeiche Ould Chighaly answering it on an amplified tidinit lute beside her. The embaire, a log xylophone from Busoga in Uganda, needs six players seated along its two sides, and the Nakibembe Xylophone Troupe lock their parts together so tightly that no single line can be picked out of the pattern. Yegor Zabelov, Belarusian and now based in Poland, takes the accordion somewhere its folk past never pointed, pulling drones and walls of noise from the bellows, and has been known to bite them to force the sound out. Few sets on the Saturday hit as hard as Jupiter & Okwess. Bokondji started the band in Kinshasa in 1990, after a childhood split between the capital and East Berlin where his father served as a diplomat, then spent years travelling Congo learning the rhythms of its hundreds of ethnic groups while the capital’s orchestras stuck to rumba. He calls the result bofenia rock, and it comes with lyrics those bands avoid: poverty, war, corruption, sung in six languages. Their fourth album Ekoya, partly recorded in Mexico with producer Camilo Lara, arrived last year. The Saturday’s line-up makes room for jazz as well, through two players who came to it from outside. Alfa Mist grew up in Newham and found jazz through the samples buried in the hip-hop he was making as a teenager, then taught himself piano to chase where they came from; the records since keep that double origin audible, boom-bap drums under voicings borrowed from Ahmad Jamal, verses he raps himself dropped between instrumentals. Leeds-born Emma-Jean Thackray came up through the London scene but her 2021 debut Yellow pulled in Afrofuturism, spiritual jazz and electronic production alongside it, and she has a MOBO and a Mercury nomination behind her. From London jazz the day moves to Portugal, and two singers working the tradition from opposite ends. Gisela João, from Barcelos in the north, sings fado the old way, Amália Rodrigues songs beside her own, and her self-titled 2013 debut went to number one at home. Three albums have followed, each further from the fado house: Nua, AuRora, and last year’s Inquieta, which reworks José Afonso and other Portuguese songbook material into new arrangements. Ana Lua Caiano works alone with a loop pedal, layering her own voice against synths, drum machines and field recordings until the rural Portuguese music her parents raised her on comes out glitchy, industrial and danceable. Her 2024 debut Vou Ficar Neste Quadrado built that method into songs that turn on group-chant vocals and a hard, clipped beat, and landed on a stack of 2024 best-of lists, with a second album due at the end of the year. Then come the big bands and bigger sounds. Mexico’s Mixanteña de Santa Cecilia, eleven women on brass and percussion, play the Pacific-coast cumbias and boleros of a banda tradition that never used to admit them. Big Pollo have spent twenty years in Lima perfecting what they call chichafunky, Peruvian psychedelic cumbia driven through hard funk. And Cotonou’s Bénin International Musical, a large collective built around Vodun rhythm and chant, set them against rock and electronics. The Shanghai Restoration Project turns the day electronic. Producer Dave Liang has spent two decades folding Chinese instrumentation into hip-hop and dance, and here he works with South African vocalist Tebza Majaivane, amapiano running underneath. That sound carries into the NTS stage after dark, where the night belongs to DJs: DJ Travella from Dar es Salaam pushing singeli past 200 beats per minute, Cheb Mimo on raï, chaabi and North African club music, and London’s Shannen SP on kuduro, gqom and amapiano. The Sunday belongs to the ‘Songbird of Wassoulou’. Oumou Sangaré has spent forty years turning the music of southern Mali into a platform against polygamy, forced marriage and female genital cutting. She was twenty-one when Moussolou came out in 1990, selling by the cassette-load across West Africa, and the arguments in her lyrics have not softened since, carried in the same voice over the kamelengoni harp. If Sangaré built her tradition into a stage, Ustad Noor Bakhsh very nearly never reached one. He had played the benju, a keyed zither the Baloch rebuilt from a Japanese children’s toy, for over fifty years on the Makran coast, mostly at weddings and healing ceremonies, when an anthropologist tracked him down beside a broken motorbike in 2022 and filmed him; the clip went round the world, and Jingul followed, recorded outdoors by a creek, the benju run through an old Philips amp he bought in a Karachi market. Another of the Sunday’s heavyweights, Garifuna Collective, exists to keep a whole culture from vanishing. The Garifuna descend from enslaved West Africans shipwrecked off St Vincent in the 1600s, who mixed with the island’s Carib people before the British exiled them to the Central American coast; their language, an Arawakan tongue threaded with African and Carib words, survives in scattered communities across Belize, Honduras and Guatemala and is now UN-listed as endangered. The Collective hold it alive the way the culture always has, through the primero and segunda drums, turtle shells and call-and-response singing, a mission the late Andy Palacio set them on with Wátina in 2007. Others take a tradition they were handed and drag it somewhere new. Dudù Kouate, born in Senegal into a griot family and long based in Bergamo, plays over two hundred traditional African instruments and has been a permanent member of the Art Ensemble of Chicago since 2017, carrying West African oral music into free jazz. Clara Serra López, London-based and of Catalan and Cuban heritage, works the other end of the same idea, a trained jazz singer threading Mediterranean ornamentation and Iberian rhythm through modular synths; her two Lengua Materna EPs on Real World turn on colonialism, migration and the cost-of-living squeeze her generation grew up inside. The pull between root and machine sharpens in two more of the day’s voices. Lebanese singer Yasmine Hamdan helped invent Arabic indie in the late nineties with the Beirut duo Soapkills, whispering classical Arabic over trip-hop beats; solo and now in Paris, she sings across Lebanese, Kuwaiti, Palestinian and Egyptian dialects in a spare, hypnotic register that owes as much to Portishead as to the Arab songbook. Galician trio Tanxugueiras, Aida Tarrío and the twins Olaia and Sabela Maneiro, do the same to the pandeireta singing of northern Spain, three voices over frame drums set against trap production; their song ‘Terra’ won the public vote at Spain’s 2022 Benidorm Fest and took a near-lost Galician tradition to a national television audience. The last day of WOMAD 26 has far more to give. Jamaica’s Hempress Sativa was grew up inside reggae. Her father, the selector Ilawi Malawi, sat her in front of the mic at his Jah Love sound-system sessions before she was five, and she grew up to sing and toast in equal measure, roots reggae in substance with a DJ’s delivery on top. Her songs run on Rastafari and resistance: African unity, Babylon and Black struggle, the sacrament of ganja, her own command of the mic. Glasgow’s corto.alto is one of the most sought-after names in UK jazz right now. Trombonist Liam Shortall leads it, writing at the desk as much as on the stand, running jazz through hip-hop, dub and club production, and his debut Bad With Names was shortlisted for the 2024 Mercury Prize. Around him he keeps a rotating Glasgow crew, the band changing shape from gig to gig, so the set is as much a snapshot of the city’s young jazz scene as a showcase of his own. Nothing on the day sounds like Japan’s Seppuku Pistols. They started as an electric punk band and, after the 2011 Fukushima disaster left them, in their words, ashamed of needing electricity to make noise, threw out their amps and switched to taiko drums, shamisen and bamboo flute. What comes out is punk played entirely on traditional instruments, a full troupe in Edo-era farm dress, as much a protest against the modern world as a gig. And after dark, Cuba’s Cami Layé Okún sees the festival out on the NTS stage. A vinyl-only selector, she runs the monthly Insolar show on NTS from Havana, where she’s the only DJ putting on all-vinyl nights, digging out Cuban disco, Afro-Caribbean rarities and tropical Amazonian grooves, records that take real effort to find on an island cut off from the global trade. Four days, a site never used for this before, and a bill running from Balochi zahirok to Japanese taiko-punk, Beninese Vodun to Peruvian chichafunky, and the world in between. That has always been the WOMAD wager, that the stranger a booking looks on paper the better it plays in a Wiltshire field, and the 2026 edition, already among the fastest-selling in the festival’s history, is that bet laid down one more time on new ground.   Weekend passes, day tickets and camping are at womad.co.uk with the 2026 edition already among the fastest-selling in the festival's history     Cover Photo ©: Ryley Morton The post Event Preview: WOMAD 2026 @ Neston Park (Corsham, Wiltshire; Thursday 23rd to Sunday 26th July 2026) appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: I wanna be happy Even if I said I could But what if I’m lonely And the darkness bleed when I shook To celebrate the release of Mouth Ulcers’ debut EP, Silent Pictures, the band has released a video for the title track directed by frontman Zak Watson. Following the spectral layering of “Space,” the London quartet now pares its visual language down to a single blue chamber, where performance, memory, and private distress are pressed into the same cold frame. The title “silent pictures” calls back to cinema before synchronized speech: an art built from faces, gestures, shadows, and the sudden eloquence of a cut. Gothic rock has long carried that visual grammar into music. The warped interiors of The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, the advancing silhouette of Nosferatu, and the deathly poise of early screen horror survive in the genre’s high-contrast lighting, looming shadows, romantic morbidity, and sense that the performer has been supernaturally summoned rather than merely photographed. Watson’s video understands that inheritance as atmosphere rather than costume. It begins in a wash of blue so dense that the band seem suspended inside a photographic negative. High contrast strips the room of softness: faces turn pale, instruments gleam, and every movement acquires the blunt clarity of evidence. The setup is simple, and Watson uses that simplicity as pressure, keeping the camera close enough to catch the musicians as they tighten around the song. Formed in London in 2025, Mouth Ulcers have moved quickly from studio experiment to sold-out rooms in Britain and the Netherlands. Across Silent Pictures, traces of Bauhaus, The Chameleons, The Damned, The Cult, and the early Horrors surface without hardening into a pastiche of these influences. Written between July 2025 and early 2026, its songs settle into distinct temperaments, united by the private ache beneath the band’s dramatic poise. The title track circles a wish for happiness that keeps collapsing into loneliness, pain, and the erosion of memory. Repetition gives time a physical presence, as though each return to the refrain has removed another object from the room. Watson sings with a restrained intensity, while Josephine Rose, Jamie-Lee Culver, and David Zbirka supply a disciplined force around him. The performance becomes an act of endurance, with four people holding their places while something inward begins to give way. “It’s music for the dark nature that’s lurking beneath the ‘perfect’ world,” says the band. “It marks just the start of how we’d like to start our journey as a band and we hope everyone enjoys listening.” The video gives gothic style the discipline of precision. Its blue palette carries emotional weight from the opening frame. It flattens distinctions between skin, fabric, wall, and metal, turning the band into figures caught inside the same cold exposure. Cuts arrive with measured sharpness. A guitar neck crosses the frame; a cymbal flashes; Rose’s presence gives the image another point of tension. The camera studies the slight strain of a mouth, the angle of a shoulder, and the instant before a drum strike lands. Watch the video for Silent Pictures below: The Silent Pictures EP presents Mouth Ulcers as a band alert to the theatrical inheritance of goth and equally attentive to bodily signs of distress. As the song closes, no cathartic gesture settles the unease; the image leaves the musicians inside their blue chamber, still playing against time. For a debut statement, the restraint is persuasive. Mouth Ulcers have found a visual language spacious enough for private dread, desire, and the slow disappearance at the song’s centre. Listen to “Silent Pictures” below and order the EP here. items._cn_summary: 伦敦四人乐队Mouth Ulcers首张EP以哥特摇滚为骨架，融合了Bauhaus、The Damnes、The Cult等前辈的视觉与听觉语法。核心单曲《Silent Pictures》围绕一个不断坍塌的愿望展开：渴望快乐却反复坠入孤独与记忆的侵蚀之中。歌词以重复结构制造时间的物质感，每一次副歌回归都像从房间里移走一件物品。Watson的演唱保持着克制的张力，Rose、Culver与Zbirka在周围提供纪律化的力度支撑，将表演转化为一种忍耐行为。音乐上避免了对影响源的简单拼贴，各首歌曲呈现出独立的气质，却被共同的内在痛感联结在一起。同步发布的MV由主唱Watson执导，以单一蓝色空间实现高对比度影像，削弱皮肤、布料、墙面与金属之间的界限，将乐队凝固在同一冷曝光之中，乐评认为这种处理让哥特风格获得了精确性的纪律。整体呈现一种年轻乐队将类型传统内化为氛围而非戏服的自觉。

items.body: Devil-M‘s “Titanomachie (The Remixes)” is out now as a digital release via Danse Macabre Records. The German gothic industrial act’s remix album reworks ten tracks from its 2025 album “Titanomachie,” with new versions from Psyclon Nine, Das Ich, Grausame Töchter and Destroy Me Again among others, plus an atmospheric instrumental edit of the ballad “Heaven.” TITANOMACHIE the Remixes by Devil-M Danse Macabre Records describes the remixer lineup as a “Who’s Who of the gothic scene.” Ten remixes on Devil-M’s ‘Titanomachie (The Remixes)’ “Titanomachie,” Devil-M’s fourth album, combined guitar-driven industrial metal with electronic and soundtrack textures and was mixed by Elmar Schmidt of Centhron, with mastering by Kristof Bathory of Dawn of Ashes. The remix album draws its full tracklist from that record. Antibody and Destroy Me Again both rework “Gott,” alongside a version by Psyclon Nine, the project fronted by Nero Bellum. Subliminal Code remixes “Komplex,” while Das Ich and Centhron each contribute a version of “Imperium.” Bitterfeld reworks both “Prometheus” and “Zyklopenkinder,” Grausame Töchter remixes “Apocalypto,” and Coma., a side-project of Devil-M’s own members, takes on “Tartarus.” The closing track is an instrumental “Heaven (Soundtrack Edit).” About Devil-M Devil-M formed in 2009 in Emden, Germany, as an industrial metal project that later grew into a full band now based in Bremen. The current line-up includes Max Meyer (vocals, percussion), Rotny Ramirez (bass), Void (guitar, backing vocals) and Julian Hemken (drums, programming). The band’s early album “Kannst Du sterben” appeared in 2011, followed by “Revenge of the Antichrist” in 2014 through Meth-Media. Devil-M issued “Hollow Earth” through darkTunes Music Group in January 2017, then signed to Danse Macabre Records for “Astharat,” released on 28 February 2020, with the remix-driven “Embryogötter” following later that year. The band’s fourth album, “Titanomachie,” arrived on 30 November 2025, preceded by the singles “Komplex” and “Olympus Ardet.” “Titanomachie (The Remixes),” released digitally on 3 July 2026, extends that album with new versions from Psyclon Nine, Das Ich, Grausame Töchter, Antibody, Destroy Me Again, Subliminal Code, Centhron, Bitterfeld and Coma.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张德国哥特工业乐队Devil-M的混音专辑，素材来自其2025年第四张专辑《Titanomachie》。原专辑将吉他驱动的工业金属与电子及电影配乐质感融合，由Centhron的Elmar Schmidt混音、Dawn of Ashes的Kristof Bathory母带处理。混音版本汇集了Psyclon Nine、Das Ich、Grausame Töchter、Centhron等十余组哥特/工业场景的艺人，对原作进行重新解构，包括对单曲《Gott》《Komplex》《Imperium》等的多版本处理，并以《Heaven》的器乐配乐版作为终曲。整体走的是场景内协作路线，多位风格相近的艺人从各自视角重新诠释同一批素材，展现了德国地下工业圈的协作生态。

items.body: Coil’s 1987 album “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” returns remastered on limited-edition vinyl, CD and digitally on 30 October 2026, released by Mute in partnership with Coil’s own imprint Threshold House. The reissue is the first in a planned series of early Coil releases and carries the catalog number COIL3. Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders) by Coil “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is the third album in a trilogy that began with “Scatology” (1984) and “Horse Rotorvator” (1986). Stephen Thrower, who joined Coil during the album’s creation, describes it as drawing on material sidelined during “Horse Rotorvator’s” sequencing, shaped into what he calls “the culmination of a ‘magnum opus’ in the artistic sense, the closure of a trilogy […] rounding up even our most jagged, cryptic, frictional, intemperate materials into a final balanced form.” The album’s field recordings include a brass band recorded in Mexico, a fragment of a British boxing documentary, and a Thai boxing arena captured by Peter Christopherson; on “Metal in the Head,” a malfunctioning hired Fairlight sampler randomly distorted the recording, and the accident was kept on the finished track. ‘Gold is the Metal’ tracklist and reissue details The remaster restores the album’s artwork, reconstructed by Thrower and his partner Ossian Brown (a member of Coil from 1999 to 2004) with additional archive material, including artefacts, photographs and personal notes by John Balance. The vinyl and CD editions carry new sleeve notes. Lead track “Cardinal Points” is streaming now as the reissue’s first single. Tracklist: 1. The Last Rites of Spring (2026 Remaster) 2. Paradisiac (2026 Remaster) 3. Thump (2026 Remaster) 4. For Us They Will (2026 Remaster) 5. The Broken Wheel (2026 Remaster) 6. Boy in a Suitcase (2026 Remaster) 7. Golden Hole (2026 Remaster) 8. Cardinal Points (2026 Remaster) 9. Red Slur (2026 Remaster) 10. …Of Free Enterprise (2026 Remaster) 11. Aqua Regalia (2026 Remaster) 12. Metal in the Head (2026 Remaster) 13. Either His, or Yours (2026 Remaster) 14. Chickenskin (2026 Remaster) 15. Soundtrap (2026 Remaster) 16. The First Five Minutes after Violent Death (2026 Remaster) Mute and Threshold House plan to follow “Gold is the Metal” with further early Coil reissues: the soundtrack for Derek Jarman’s “The Angelic Conversation,” the previously unreleased music Coil recorded for Clive Barker’s “Hellraiser,” and the compilation “Unnatural History.” About Coil Coil formed in London in 1982 as a solo project of John Balance (born Geoffrey Burton, 1962-2004), then a member of Psychic TV. The project became a duo when Balance’s partner Peter “Sleazy” Christopherson (1955-2010), formerly of Throbbing Gristle, joined him. Coil’s first release, the one-sided 12″ single “How to Destroy Angels,” came out in 1984. Stephen Thrower joined the group during the recording of “Horse Rotorvator” (1986) and remained through “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” (1987), the third and closing album of a trilogy that also included “Scatology” (1984). Coil released music through the 1990s and 2000s that ranged from the industrial dance of “Windowpane” to the ambient “Time Machines” (1998) and the two-volume “Musick to Play in the Dark.” John Balance died in 2004 after a fall at the band’s home, and Coil effectively ended; Peter Christopherson continued to oversee reissues of the group’s catalog until his own death in 2010. Ossian Brown, a member of Coil from 1999 to 2004, has worked with Thrower on multiple archival reissues since, including releases on Cold Spring and Dais Records. Side-Line has covered several recent Coil reissues, including the expanded edition of Coil’s “Hellraiser” sessions in 2026, the 10th-anniversary “Backwards” reissue via Cold Spring, and the 25th-anniversary edition of Icon of Coil’s “Serenity is the Devil.” “Gold is the Metal (With the Broadest Shoulders)” is the first release in the new Mute and Threshold House partnership, reactivating Coil’s own imprint under Thrower and Brown’s stewardship in association with the estates of Balance and Christopherson.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非传统乐评，而是一篇关于Coil 1987年专辑再版发行的新闻稿。专辑是Coil早期三部曲的终章，素材源自《Horse Rotorvator》录制期间的边角料，经整理后形成一个完整作品。录制中大量使用田野录音，包括墨西哥铜管乐队、英国拳击纪录片片段以及泰国拳击场实况，Fairlight采样器的故障被刻意保留在成品中。Stephen Thrower将专辑描述为将所有尖锐、隐晦、不羁的材料汇聚为平衡终章的艺术尝试。再版由Mute与Coil旗下Threshold House合作发行，封面艺术由Thrower与Ossian Brown根据John Balance的档案资料重建，后续还将发行更多Coil早期作品再版。文章信息集中在发行细节与创作背景，缺少对音乐本身听觉特征的分析与评价。

items.body: “Trace” marks the third album by the Greek duo Incirrina. George Katsanos and Irini Tiniakou have crafted 11 tracks that naturally continue the musical direction established on their previous releases. We are treated to a collection of well-crafted Electro-Wave compositions, distinguished above all by superb vintage synth sounds. These warm, analog textures create a captivating listening experience. The music is highly danceable, with several tracks even embracing a distinct club-oriented feel. Although the album also features a handful of more atmospheric and melancholic moments, its greatest strength lies in the harder, dance-driven songs. The vocal delivery occasionally recalls that of their compatriots Paradox Obscur, sharing a similarly detached yet sensual approach that perfectly complements the music’s atmosphere. A particularly nice touch is the closing track, performed in Greek, which provides a memorable conclusion to the album. “Trace” is an infectious and accomplished release from a band that had already shown considerable promise. Offering greater variety than its predecessors, it successfully blends different influences into a cohesive, engaging, and highly enjoyable whole. (Rating:8). Listen to “Presence”: Presence by Incirrina About Incirrina Incirrina is a dark electronic and minimal synth duo based in Athens, Greece, consisting of George Katsanos (synthesizers, drum machine, waterphone, vocals) and Irini Tiniakou (synthesizers, vocals). The band has played gigs and festivals in Greece, Germany, Belgium, Hungary, and Croatia, including Pliisken Festival, Morphic Festival, Cold Transmission Festival, and Death Disco Festival – The Warm Up, and has opened for Front 242 and Ambassade. Incirrina released its first LP, “8.15”, in 2019 through Geheimnis Records, followed by the digital maxi single “Utter” in 2020 and the split maxi single “Devastations / R.Daneel” with The Man & His Failures in 2021 via Smash Records. The second LP, “Lip Led Scream”, followed in 2022 on Cold Transmission, and the double single “Immersion” arrived in 2024 on the same label. The band’s third album, “Trace”, was released through Cold Transmission Music.
items._cn_summary: Incirrina的第三张专辑《Trace》由希腊双人组George Katsanos与Irini Tiniakou创作，包含11首曲目。专辑延续了前作奠定的电子浪潮方向，以温暖模拟合成器音色为核心特征，营造出引人入胜的听感体验。作品整体偏向舞曲化，其中多首曲目呈现俱乐部取向，同时穿插部分氛围阴郁、深沉忧郁的段落。人声演绎疏离而感性，与音乐氛围相得益彰。希腊语演唱的收尾曲为整张专辑画上独特句点。相比前作，本作在多样性上有所提升，将不同影响融合为一个连贯的整体，既适合舞池也适合静听，展现了乐队从潜力走向成熟的完整面貌。

items.body: Jah Wobble and Tian Qiyi released “Strawberry Fields Forever” on July 14, 2026, the second single from their album “Mystic Liverpool: The Beatles’ Psychedelic Psongbook”, due August 14 via Cherry Red Records and Wobble’s own label 30 Hertz. The track is available on Spotify and Apple Music. “Strawberry Fields Forever” reworks the Beatles’ 1967 song around Charlie Wardle’s morin khuur playing and vocals, joined by his mother Zi Lan Liao, a Royal Academy of Music-trained harpist and guzheng player, on guzheng. John T Wardle contributes drums and yangqin, and Jah Wobble plays dub bass throughout. Jah Wobble, John T and Charlie jointly produced the track, which John T recorded and mixed at Pagoda Studios in Liverpool, where Tian Qiyi is now based. Jah Wobble & Tian Qiyi on ‘Strawberry Fields Forever’ Jah Wobble called the song the record he grew up with in London’s East End and described it as the natural centrepiece of “Mystic Liverpool”: “This is the one that started everything for me – the song that opened my psyche as a small boy in the East End. So it was always going to be the centrepiece of this record. It’s a family track in every sense with Charlie on erhu, morin khuur and vocals, John T on drums and yangqin, and Zi Lan on guzheng. The dub sensibility runs right through it – there’s a lot of space in the mix, a lot of trust in the listener. I don’t think we’ve tried to compete with the original. What we’ve done, I hope, is honour the mystery of it – let it breathe in a slightly different room, with different instruments, and see what happens. It still feels like more than music to me.” Charlie Wardle, who plays erhu and morin khuur on the track, linked the arrangement to the song’s own subject matter: “This is a song about a real place Lennon remembered from childhood, and the erhu suits that kind of homesickness really well. We didn’t try to be clever with it – we just played the melody like we meant it.” John T Wardle, who recorded and mixed the track, explained the choice to build a dense arrangement rather than a straight cover: “Everyone knows this song, so there was no point in doing a straight cover. We made a conscious choice to go for a massive, hypnotic wall of sound. We brought our mum in to layer up these beautiful, cascading textures on the guzheng, Charlie’s driving the melody on his strings, and then dad and I just locked in to create this heavy, deep groove on the bass and drums. It’s less of a tribute and more of a dark, trippy, out-there collision of our family’s two musical worlds.” “Strawberry Fields Forever” follows the album’s lead single, “Tomorrow Never Knows”, released on June 16, 2026 with an accompanying visualizer. Jah Wobble & Tian Qiyi’s ‘Mystic Liverpool’ album “Mystic Liverpool: The Beatles’ Psychedelic Psongbook” reworks ten songs from the Beatles’ psychedelic period: “Tomorrow Never Knows”, “Strawberry Fields Forever”, “Within You Without You”, “I Am The Walrus”, “Norwegian Wood”, “Blue Jay Way”, “The Inner Light”, “Love You To”, “Flying” and “Rain”. Jah Wobble plays dub bass throughout, John T Wardle plays drums, Chinese percussion and yangqin, and Charlie Wardle plays erhu and morin khuur and sings. Cherry Red Records and 30 Hertz release the album on August 14, 2026 as a CD digipak and digitally. The album is dedicated to Zi Lan Liao’s father, Mr K.H. Li (Liao Gui Xiong), who arrived in Liverpool from Guangzhou in 1981 as Chinese Cultural Officer at the Pagoda and went on to found the Pagoda Chinese Youth Orchestra. Zi Lan Liao, now director of the Pagoda Arts Centre, runs the orchestra, in which both her sons played from the age of three. About Jah Wobble & Tian Qiyi Jah Wobble, born John Joseph Wardle on August 11, 1958 in Stepney, East London, became the original bass player of Public Image Ltd (PiL), the band John Lydon formed after the Sex Pistols split. Wobble played on “Public Image: First Issue” (1978) and “Metal Box” (1979) before a falling-out with Lydon led to his departure in 1980. He went on to collaborate with Holger Czukay and Jaki Liebezeit of CAN, U2’s The Edge and producer Francois Kevorkian on the 1983 LP “Snake Charmer”. In 1982 he formed Jah Wobble’s Invaders of the Heart, and the group’s 1991 album “Rising Above Bedlam” brought Wobble his commercial peak and a Mercury Music Prize nomination, spawning the UK top-40 single “Visions of You” featuring Sinead O’Connor. His 1994 album “Take Me to God” featured Baaba Maal, Dolores O’Riordan and Chaka Demus. Over a five-decade career Wobble has also recorded with Massive Attack, Ginger Baker, Björk, Brian Eno and Pharoah Sanders, and in 2009 he won a Songlines Music Award with the Chinese Dub Orchestra for the album “Chinese Dub”, a collaboration with his wife, guzheng player and harpist Zi Lan Liao. He now runs his own label, 30 Hertz Records. Side-Line has followed his recent collaborations, including Horace Andy on “Timeless Roots”, Ken Boothe on “Old Fashioned Ways”, and former Siouxsie and the Banshees guitarist Jon Klein on the album “Automated Paradise” (previewed by “Who Wins?”). Tian Qiyi takes its name from the Chinese middle names of John T Wardle and Charlie Wardle, Tian Qi and Tian Yi. The Liverpool-based brothers grew up playing in their grandfather’s Pagoda Chinese Youth Orchestra and bridge British, Chinese, Mongolian and dub traditions with post-punk and experimental production. “Tomorrow Never Knows”, released June 16, 2026, was the first record to bring Jah Wobble together with his sons under the Tian Qiyi name. “Strawberry Fields Forever” is their second single together, ahead of the full “Mystic Liverpool: The Beatles’ Psychedelic Psongbook” album on August 14, 2026. Jah Wobble & Tian Qiyi tour dates 2026 Jah Wobble & Tian Qiyi perform together on: August 15, 2026 – Suffield Summer Fiesta, The Suffield Arms (UK) Jah Wobble and The Invaders of the Heart also tour the UK and Belgium through the rest of 2026: October 3 – Stourbridge, Katie Fitzgerald’s (UK) October 16 – Todmorden, Unitarian Church (UK) October 21 – Frome, The Tunnels (UK) October 22 – Bristol, The Fleece (UK) October 23 – Reading, The Face Bar (UK) November 7 – London, Bush Hall (UK) November 25 – Hasselt, Club AFF (Belgium) November 26 – Bruges, Cactus (Belgium) November 27 – Oudenaarde, Harmonie (Belgium) Tickets are available via jahwobble.com.

items._cn_summary: Jah Wobble与田七伊合作专辑《Mystic Liverpool: The Beatles' Psychedelic Psongbook》是对披头士作品的重新诠释。《Strawberry Fields Forever》以马头琴、二胡和古筝等中国及蒙古传统乐器为核心，Charlie Wardle的演唱与器乐演奏贯穿全曲，Jah Wobble的dub贝斯线构建低频基底，制作人John T Wardle采用'催眠式音墙'手法，刻意避开直白的翻唱路线。该作品的创作背景为家族协作，母亲Zi Lan Liao的古筝层叠营造出绵密的东方音色纹理，与披头士原曲的迷幻主题形成跨文化对话。整体定位介于世界音乐融合与实验性改编之间，独立厂牌Cherry Red和30 Hertz发行，保留了地下制作的空间感与实验余地。

items.body: 調布国際音楽祭2026権代敦彦 オペラ《ZEN》 Chofu International Music FestivalZEN 2026年6月26日（金）19:00開演（ゲネプロ取材：6月25日） 調布市文化会館たづくり くすのきホール 2026/6/26 Chofu City Cultural Center Tazukuri Kusunoki Hall Text＆Photos by 長澤直子（Naoko Nagasawa）   権代敦彦 オペラ《ZEN》 作曲：権代敦彦 脚本：堤春恵 演出：田尾下哲 指揮：鈴木優人 鈴木大拙：加耒徹（バリトン）西田幾多郎：与那城敬（バリトン）木村和夫：櫻田亮（テノール）鷹野清：加藤宏隆（バスバリトン）木村正子：村松稔之（カウンターテナー）看守：渡辺祐介（バス） 尺八：黒田鈴尊 管弦楽・男声合唱：バッハ・コレギウム・ジャパン 照明：稲葉直人美術：杉浦充ヘアメイク：原美沙紀 バッハ・コレギウム・ジャパン テノール：近野桂介、谷口洋介、中嶋克彦、水越啓バス：大井哲也、小池優介、氷見健一郎、渡辺祐介リコーダー：譜久島彰フラウトトラヴェルソ：菅きよみヴァイオリン：原田陽ヴィオラ：高岸卓人チェロ：山本徹バロックハープ：伊藤美恵チェンバロ：辛川太一オルガン：石丸由佳バロックティンパニ：菅原淳 調布国際音楽祭は、東京都調布市で毎年初夏に開催される、クラシック音楽を中心とした国際音楽祭である。主な会場となる調布市グリーンホールや調布市文化会館たづくりのほか、市内各所でもコンサートや教育プログラム、無料イベントが開催され、地域と音楽が一体となる音楽祭として親しまれている。2013年からは、調布市出身の鈴木優人がエグゼクティブ・プロデューサーを務めている。 2026年は6月20日〜28日に開催されたが、そのプログラムの中でも最大の話題となり注目を集めたのが、権代敦彦作曲によるオペラ《ZEN》の世界初演だ。約500席のくすのきホールで一度限り上演された本作。チケットの売れ行きも好調で、完売となっていたようだ。本稿では、本番を前に行われたゲネプロの模様を紹介する。   《ZEN》の舞台となるのは、第二次世界大戦前夜から戦後。主な登場人物は、禅の思想を世界へ広めた鈴木大拙（加耒徹）と哲学者の西田幾多郎（与那城敬）、戦争に翻弄される軍医の鷹野清（加藤宏隆）と学徒兵の木村和夫（櫻田亮）、そして木村の妹正子（村松稔之）。出演する歌手は、女性役を含め全てが男性。合唱も男声のみで構成されていた。 オーケストラは、各パート一人ずつという削ぎ落とされた編成で、舞台手前の位置に配置された。冒頭では、男声合唱もオーケストラに溶け込むように下手に位置し、それらを囲む形で舞台が組まれていた。 舞台装置は用いられず、光と影の効果によって人物の心情を描き出すという、抽象的とも取れるもの。とりわけ印象的だったのは、舞台中央の背景に浮かび上がる円である。この円は第一幕では四角であり、第二幕の始めではほんの小さな点であった。それが場面を追うごとに拡大して行き、最後には巨大な満月のような、あるいは禅の「円相」を思わせる光となる。そして物語の最後は読経のような響きと、一本の尺八（黒田鈴尊）の音色により収斂していく。 この作品は、一度の鑑賞ですべてを理解できるとは言えないかもしれない。しかし、男声だけで紡がれる緊張感、指揮の鈴木優人率いるバッハ・コレギウム・ジャパンの精緻な演奏、そして尺八が導く終幕は、世界初演にふさわしい、忘れがたい体験として心に残るものとなったのではないだろうか。 （2026.7.15） 作曲：権代敦彦（中央左）／脚本：堤春恵（中央右）

items._cn_summary: 本文报道调布国际音乐祭2026年权代敦彦作曲歌剧《ZEN》的世界首演。作品以二战前后为背景，聚焦铃木大拙、西田幾多郎等禅学与哲学人物，男性歌手（甚至含女角）与男声合唱构成全部声部。乐队为巴洛克编制，由铃木优人指挥巴赫合奏团日本分团演绎，融入尺八这一传统乐器。舞台以光影替代布景，背景中象征圆相的圆光由第一幕的方形逐渐扩展为满月，结尾以诵经式音响与尺八收束。在精简化编制与禅意舞台意象之间，展现传统与现代的融合，但评论以报道与赏析为主，原创洞见较为有限。

items.body:
Strong new doublepack from Short Span’s increasingly prolific Natal Zaks aka Picture, following his excellent ‘Eeeeeeee’ label debut with a new set of driving, swinging specials, tipped FFO Convextion, Plastikman, Shinichi Atobe, Miles Demdike.

‘Uuuuuuuu’ follows suit from ‘Eeeeeeee’ with six distinctively brisk, detailed and aerated swingers ranging from crispy, tracky jack-tracks to friskier chord riders well poised for various points of the night. The mesmerising whisk of ‘Quuuuuuu’ sets up a dead strong suite taking in swingeing techno-house on ‘Ruuuuu’, and Brinkmann-meets-Grungerman hypnosis of ‘Miiiiiii’, whilst the frothing ‘Leeeeeee’ gets right under the skin like some Shinichi Atobe-meets-Convextion special for Chain Reaction, and the hardgroovers get served with friskiest shake of ‘Wooooooo’.

Yyyyyyyyy is also on the way, collect them all!
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Picture（Short Span旗下）的全新双碟发行，延续了前作'Eeeeeeee'的路线，收录六首节奏鲜明、细节丰富且透气感强的舞曲作品。整体风格在techno-house与deep house之间游走，既有干脆利落的jack-track节奏骨架，也有更具探索性的和弦推进。单曲'Quuuuuuu'以迷人的质感开场，'Ruuuuu'呈现强劲摇摆的techno-house律动，'Miiiiiii'带有Brinkmann与Grungerman式的催眠氛围，'Leeeeeee'深潜入皮肤之下，呼应Shinichi Atobe与Convextion为Chain Reaction打造的私密质感，'Wooooooo'则为偏好硬派groove的听众提供最锐利的律动冲击。整张专辑定位为夜间俱乐部场景的多时段实用工具，FFO指向清晰，制作严谨但未表现出极端实验性。

items.body:
A second pressing of last year’s gorgeous fourth and final album from Old Saw, the American Primitive project of Tongue Depressor's Henry Birdsey, riffing on the classic Takoma paradigm with additional ferric washes and layered instrumental drones, huge recommendation if yr into Bruce Langhorne’s ‘The Hired Hand’ or classic work by Daniel Lanois, Laraaji, Pelt, Stars Of The Lid, State River Widening.

'The Wringing Cloth' is Birdsey’s fourth and final Old Saw outing, and ironically it’s also the one that has garnered most amount of critical and commercial success. Old Saw’s shimmering, drone-heavy soundscapes were recorded on 1/4" tape at various locations in New England over the last few years and are once again paired with evocative black and white imagery from photographer Dylan Hausthor, whose landscapes somehow perfectly capture the timeless, widescreen appeal of the music inside.

Birdsey's pedal, lap steel and resonator are at the core of each track, but the album also features Old Saw’s usual personnel; Harper Reed on nylon string guitar and banjo, Ira Dorset on fiddle and bowed strings, Ann Rowlis on reed organ and harmonium, Jim Cutler on telecaster, Addison Starkweather-Price on bass, and Peter Catchpole on metal objects and power hammer. That lap steel lends the music its stylistic anchor, taking us through decades of American folk before gently fraying at the edges. Birdsey's application of classical minimalism - the themes that surge through his work with Zach Rowden as Tongue Depressor - is still somehow present here, especially as the record pulls into its second side and the shimmering country-fied atmosphere is pierced with bell-like sounds, but the overall mood and flavour of the record is distinctly easy on the ear and timeless in its appeal.

As the label put it, “What has always been uncanny about this music is that it arrives in a state at once familiar and obscured, like a memory weighed down with sensory information but no identifying details to place it. The Wringing Cloth walks off further into that geographical dream without time or language, until it’s just a speck of light….”
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Henry Birdsey（同时运营Tongue Depressor项目）Old Saw系列的第四张也是最后一张作品，已在美国新英格兰地区的多个地点使用1/4英寸磁带录制完成。核心乐器包括踏板滑棒吉他、膝上滑棒和共鸣器吉他，配合竖琴吉他、班卓琴、小提琴、管风琴、特雷琴和贝斯等乐器，金属物体与电锤的运用为音景增添了独特的质感和厚度。专辑以美国原始吉他流派（Takoma学派）为根基，穿插经典极简主义主题的影响，磁带录音带来特有的温暖噪音和铁磁质感。音乐在数十年的美国民谣传统中穿行，滑棒吉他构成风格锚点，但声音会在边缘逐渐模糊溶解。后半段闪烁的乡村氛围被钟声般的音色刺穿，形成层次丰富的听觉体验。整张专辑呈现一种既熟悉又模糊的听觉状态，如同一段充满感官信息却无法定位的记忆。

items.body:
Sickest Dagbani dance-pop from northern Ghana, all produced by Mohamed “Ebony” Fuseini of Studio Simpa, and voiced by Dickson Gawani, Bala Zaaku, and Yaa Naara, among others - FFO DJ Tobzy, DJ Diaki, Nozinja, Music From Saharan WhatsApp

Issued on the Autotune The World label that shares its name with Chris Kirkley's long-running NTS show, ‘Digital Dance Music on VCD from Dagbon, Northern Ghana’ follows the show and label’s hyper-specific focus on the likes of Tecnobrega from Brasil and Caribbean Soca & Chutney with a rare jag upcountry in Ghana’s predominantly Muslim north. 

Armed with phone mic, FL Studio, and the best local singers on speed dial, Mohamed “Ebony” Fuseini updates local styles of Dagbani dance rhythm and melody with shiny VSTs and, of course, nuff autotune, to bring the rural sound closer to those from bigger cities, as heard on shared mp3s and physical media such as VCDs.

Available and traded at local markets, but rarely heard by international ears, those VCDs feature footage of women shaking hips - a “light cultural transgression” in the mostly Muslim area - with lyrics by local “Gawani”, flashy singers such as Dickson Gawani, Bala Zaaku, and Yaa Naara, with something to show, and matched by the energy of Ebony’s productions. Not as rushy as, say DJ Tobzy from Lagos, or DJ Diaki in Mali, Ebony’s Studio Simpa cuts are more melodic, pop-wise, maybe best compared with the colourful hi-energy of Shangaan Electro, heard on highlights from Dickson Gawani’s acidic percolator ‘So Tinha’ (also in a killer 12” bonus mix!), thru the lilting ballad ‘Baamunu’ by Obaako, to the unique skank of Aminu Dakogu, and the supremely light-headed effect of ‘M Be Adama’ by Alhassan Kukuonaa - all primed to light a fire on summer ’26 ‘floors.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦加纳北部达贡地区的VCD舞蹈音乐，制作人Mohamed "Ebony" Fuseini以Studio Simpa为基地，用手机麦克风、FL Studio与丰富的VST插件改造当地达贡巴舞蹈节奏，加入大量autotune处理，使原本乡村的声音更贴近城市审美。专辑在Autotune The World厂牌发行，延续了该厂牌对全球边缘流行声音的关注路线。演唱者包括Dickson Gawani、Bala Zaaku、Yaa Naara等本地歌手，歌词以豪萨语及达贡巴语为主，内容常涉及女性舞动身体等在当地带有文化越界意味的主题。音乐风格介于旋律化流行与电子节拍之间，与DJ Tobzy、DJ Diaki等非洲电子制作人形成对照，更贴近Shangaan Electro的明亮高能质感。整体呈现出非洲都市化进程中被数字化转译的本土流行形态，具有鲜明的人类学与音乐地理学价值。

items.body:
An extra sugary batch of queer cult pop fancies on Cairo’s ever-wonderful Nashazphone label; super melodic, passionate synth-pop songs about boys, beauty and the melancholy of youth, tipped for fans of Elli et Jacno, Taxi Girl and Mathematiques Modernes.

‘Hélas’ collects 15 songs from the repertoire of Neoboris, an infamous Bordeaux/Pau duo highly active in the late ‘90s and early ‘00s. Drawing on direct Punk, Wave, Rave Culture and “Variété Française” influences, it functions as a perfect time capsule of a very specific era and mood: a boy-and-girl duo celebrating their love for boys, with melancholy and beauty.

"The origin story reads like an archetype, but the details make it sting. One half of Neoboris came out of hardcore raves and Bordeaux punk bands, carrying the raw‑throated urgency of that milieu; the other, Boris, grew up on New Wave and goth, a born songwriter whose melancholic streak ran as deep as his knack for hooks. Together they found a common altar in Elli et Jacno, Taxi Girl, Mathématiques Modernes – that peculiarly French intersection where cheap drum machines, fragile synth lines and deadpan vocals can suddenly break your heart. Out of that devotion came a duo aesthetic: compact songs, simple structures, lyrics that flirt with kitsch and then side‑step into something sharper, all delivered with the kind of chemistry you can’t rehearse into existence.

Their shows were wild in the way that only under‑funded, over‑feeling gigs can be: feedback squeal, rushed tempos, voices occasionally cracking, the two of them radiating that mix of shyness and bravado you get when you’re singing your secrets out loud. Hélas gathers the studio and home‑recorded echoes of that era and orders them into an emotional arc – from rush to comedown, infatuation to regret, celebration to elegy. The production sits right on the fault line between DIY and pop: drum machines slightly out of time, synth presets pushed into unexpected shapes, guitars toggling between brittle and blissed, all wrapped around melodies that would sound just as right on a transistor radio as in a squat.

The shadow that hangs over the record is Boris’s death in 2008, a break so abrupt it turned the entire project into unfinished business. The surviving member’s decision to keep singing these songs “everywhere I can” isn’t nostalgia, it’s a refusal to let that voice vanish into footnote status. Hélas makes that refusal tangible: 15 tracks that re‑situate Neoboris not as local cult trivia but as part of a larger, messy history of queer‑coded, under‑the‑radar French pop. You hear the mourning in the title, of course, but the music itself leans hard into joy – messy, melancholy, shoulder‑to‑shoulder joy, the kind you find on cramped dance floors at four in the morning. Singing with him then, now, and forever: Hélas documents that promise in all its scruffy, luminous detail."

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了九十年代末至两千年代初活跃于法国波尔多与 Pau 的二人组 Neoboris 的十五首作品，混合了朋克、冷波、锐舞文化与法语香颂的脉络。制作停留在 DIY 与流行之间：鼓机节拍偶尔脱拍，合成器预设被推向意料之外的形态，吉他时而脆弱时而迷离，旋律却依旧简练而抓耳。歌词游走于媚俗与锋利之间，主题围绕少年之爱、忧郁与美的消逝展开。专辑因成员 Boris 于 2008 年离世而带有悼念意味，但音乐本身更倾向于拥抱混乱而炽热的欢愉，展现了法国地下酷儿流行场景中一个独特切片的情感轨迹。Nashazphone 为开罗独立厂牌，赋予发行以跨地域的文化坐标。

items.body:
Forever Records reissue Fila Brazillia's Old Codes New Chaos, newly mastered from the original mixdowns.

"Striking the sweet spot between sampledelic downtempo and earth-rooted deep house, Fila Brazillia’s Old Codes New Chaos is a maverick patchwork of grooves and soundscapes crafted in North East England, a cult classic suite spanning deep house, broken beat and ambient shot through with wry humour.

Last physically released in limited quantities in 2002, Forever Records are revisiting this 1994 gem with an extensive reissue led by a triple vinyl pressing, newly mastered from the original mixdowns. 

Forever Records is a reissue series dedicated to rediscovering lost musical treasures from across the spectrum of head-feeding, heart-rending electronic music.. Established by Rush Hour co-founder Christiaan Macdonald and Delsin founder Marsel van der Wielen."
items._genre: downtempo / deep house / broken beat / ambient
items._cn_summary: 这张1994年的专辑由英国东北部的Fila Brazillia创作，是采样驱动的downtempo与扎根土壤的deep house之间的交汇点。整张作品像一张拼贴画，融合了deep house、broken beat与ambient等多种元素，节奏编排富于变化，音色层次带有幽默感与实验性。2026年由Forever Records重新发行，从原始混音母带重新制作母带处理，并以三张黑胶形式呈现。Forever Records由Rush Hour联合创始人Christiaan Macdonald与Delsin创始人Marsel van der Wielen创立，专注于重新发掘电子音乐领域中被遗忘的佳作。原版仅在2002年以极少量实体发行，此次的扩展再版为这张cult classic提供了重见天日的机会。

items.body: Once in a while, we realize we’ve created a closed loop. In 2023, when ACL reviewed ALT (Abby Lee Tee)’s Disputed Territory and the single “Beavers,” we lamented that “Beavers” was not on the album. Rising to the challenge, ALT has now responded with an all-beaver EP, to which (you knew this was coming) we respond, “now we’d like an all-beaver album.” And once we get it, we’re going to ask for a double album, and then a box set, and then another box set with only 45s. It’s never going to end. And that’s okay, because Abby Lee Tee loves these industrious mammals, and so do we. “Have you seen “Hoppers”? I asked ALT. He certainly had, and unveiled the fact that Emily Fairfax, whose quotes populate the EP, was the animated movie’s scientific supervisor. So there you have it; the entire universe is aligned. Our description of the original track: “Beavers” is not on the EP, but it should be. The new ALT template is established in a humorous fashion, with dialogue samples, hip-hop snippets, cutting and scratching, and the most fun since the heyday of Kid Koala. After hearing some beaver facts and quotable lines (“That doesn’t stop beavers!”), accompanied by “Come on”s, the track launches into field recordings (dam!) and a longer hip-hop quote (“Slow the flow, relax your mind, gain control, take your time”), which is of course a description of what beavers do. Then some actual beavers. This ridiculously joyful track now closes the EP, save for some bonus non-beaver tracks (more on this later). But there’s plenty of fun to precede it. ALT has clearly been as busy as a … well, you know. The title track begins with backward masking, bubbling, and busy beaver beats. “Beavers help us,” a narrator intones, which sounds like a prayer before the sentence is completed. A great respect is shown to these large-toothed builders. Fairfax’s words are chopped up like chewable logs and re-presented in stacked fashion as the workers giggle in the distance. Then the lovely piano-led trip-hop of “It’s Beautiful,” which sounds like the work of DJ Beaver Shadow, replete with tiny shavings of rap samples. The water continues to flow as the local birds offer commentary. “Redeveloping That Ecosystem” echoes the message of “Hoppers,” providing a positive path forward. And then “That Dam,” which inspires in this reviewer what he hopes will be a healthy aside. A number of years ago, I attended a speech on the topic of dams. The presenter was introduced by a teenager who lacked homonym awareness, saying, “and now he’s going to speak about his damn project.” “That Dam” reclaims the homonym from its earlier hip-hop context, reversing the teen’s misunderstanding, transforming damn to dam. “That dam is made of sticks and stones and mud … dam it! Dam right!” The 2024 oddball indie comedy “Hundreds of Beavers” was amusing, but this is funny. But wait, there’s more! If you order now, you’ll also receive, at no extra charge, three bonus non-beaver tracks! And let’s not hear any complaints like “Where are the beavers? There ought to be beavers,” because these are gifts from the artist, and you shouldn’t look a gift beaver in the mouth. You probably shouldn’t look any beaver in the mouth, unless you are a beaver dentist. The sound of running water, along with some very beaver-like sighs and barks in “The Music,” connects these pieces to the larger work. “Music” is the quintessential sampling, self-referential hip-hop track, containing samples about turntablism itself, while the closing MC quote of “Hydrology” is “like to study my flows,” which in its original context was about rhyme and in its current context is about streams. When beavers ask, “How many streams will this get?” they are talking about something else, which is the clever glory of this EP; humans are involved, but they’re not the main characters. (Richard Allen)

items._cn_summary: ALT的这张EP以河狸为主题展开音乐叙事，将对话采样、嘻哈片段、刮碟技巧与田野录音编织在一起，形成一种幽默而活泼的拼贴风格。作品围绕河狸生态展开，包含倒放处理、钢琴主导的trip-hop段落以及环境音景，鸟类鸣叫与水流声贯穿始终。制作人引用河狸专家Emily Fairfax的言论作为叙述骨架，将科普内容与节奏实验结合。整体呈现出对河狸这种生物的热爱与敬意，同时在声音设计上有一定的趣味性与创意，但风格更偏向嘻哈采样拼贴而非深度的实验电子或前卫即兴。

items.album: PREMIATA FORNERIA MARCONI (PFM) Storia Di Un Minuto (Rock Progressivo Italiano, 1972)
items.excerpt: Review by Fercandio46 — From their beginnings linked to the Battisti-Mogol project, which aimed to modernize Italian music and saw them leave their mark on recordings by Lucio Battisti and Mina Mazzini between 1969 and 1972, to taking their name from the early 20th-century bakery ("Premiata Panetteria Marconi") where they rehearsed in the basement, and serving as the opening act for Yes during the band's first Italian tour at Lyric Theatre of Milano in 1971... that is how Premiata Forneria
items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — From their beginnings linked to the Battisti-Mogol project, which aimed to modernize Italian music and saw them leave their mark on recordings by Lucio Battisti and Mina Mazzini between 1969 and 1972, to taking their name from the early 20th-century bakery ("Premiata Panetteria Marconi") where they rehearsed in the basement, and serving as the opening act for Yes during the band's first Italian tour at Lyric Theatre of Milano in 1971... that is how Premiata Forneria Marconi was born.The magic begins the moment the first notes are Heard, the magic of true classics. The guitar, the Mellotron, the mastery of silence, and the voice standing alone, singing in the language of opera. The bass and the flute... giving way to an explosion of drums and Minimoog, pure symphonic rock, with raw, palpable lyricism. Franz Di Cioccio had a distinctive way of playing the drums, syncopated, accentuating every moment of the song. Franco Mussida's voice fills Impressioni di Settembre, accompanied by drum beats fit for royalty... and then, as the tempo slows, a song emerges that feels almost like a street ballad, bohemian in spirit, a bold statement from the very start, destined to leave a mark and set a precedent for this quintet that would truly make history.With "E' Festa," the fusion of rock and symphonic styles continued, marked by a simplicity that makes it a prime example of symbiosis, where the Minimoog crowns and joins the guitar, transforming the rock sound into classical music without losing any of its energy or provocative edge."Dove... Quando... (Part I)" is so deeply imbued with the spirit of the Renaissance and Italian medieval music, featuring a polyphony only they could achieve, that listening to it feels like stepping back into that era. This first part serves as an introduction, presenting the same melody that the second part would later develop in a symphonic style; that melody is revisited in "Dove... Quando... (Part II)" by the organ and violin, which sustain it in the air until the classical piano bursts in, joined by the drums in a moment that felt remarkably modern, predating even the time when Rick Wakeman had Bill Bruford play drums alongside the organ on The Six Wives of Henry VIII.Mauro Pagani's violin joins the Minimoog on a low note until a saloon piano takes a jazzy turn; then, the vast Italian palette, with its myriad colors, comes into play alongside the flute, forming a jazz trio with enviable swing. Things turn atonal with the organ work of La Carrozza di Hans; the richness and variety of instruments at their disposal offered so many interpretive possibilities, yet none of that would have mattered without their compositional skills, it was the combination of all these elements that made the quintet work and allowed it to deliver its best.There is a Steve Hackett-esque classical guitar moment with Franco Mussida that then accelerates as they shift back into a jazz style alongside the violin; that wild, Renaissance-era, courtly past resurfaces, it was in their DNA, something these twenty-somethings carried within them, just like their generation as a whole, and they demonstrated it through their playing and composition. Then they turn funky... and "Grazie Davvero" marks the end of this auspicious beginning, the start of a bumpy, winding journey that would see them become one of the peninsula's most beloved and memorable bands.The orchestra and its wind section provided the final touch needed to conclude this debut with the grandeur it deserved, masterfully composed, constantly surprising, constantly dazzling... the same notes brought to life by piano, bass, and flute... and it matters not if rain falls upon us, as they sang there, because Premiata Forneria Marconi will be with us forever.

items._cn_summary: 这张1972年的意大利前卫摇滚专辑展现了丰富的器乐层次与跨风格融合。乐队以古典吉他、提琴、风琴、小号与Minimoog合成器为核心，将意大利文艺复兴与中世纪复调元素融入摇滚结构，同时穿插爵士钢琴段落和无调性管风琴即兴。鼓手Franz Di Cioccio以切分节奏驱动情绪起伏，吉他手Franco Mussida的人声在抒情段落中呈现近乎波西米亚的街谣气质。专辑的多乐章作品如《Dove... Quando...》分两部分展开，先以中世纪复调铺垫旋律主题，后由管风琴、小提琴和钢琴将其发展为交响摇滚框架。整体呈现出古典、爵士与摇滚三者的有机共生，在意大利前卫摇滚场景中具有开创性意义。

items.body: Review by alainPP — This is the second album in a trilogy marking the band's return after a long hiatus'their eighth overall'exploring the group's inner journey through a gothic-prog lens."Sanguis" opens with Endre's nostalgic vintage organ, Kjetil's baritone vocals, and a fluid heavy riff that is neither pompous nor solemn. It evolves into a groovy, hypnotic, and majestic soundscape, joined by screamed vocals. The lyrics'dealing with domestic violence and its bloody aftermath'steer the music between light and dark, bridging the gap between atmospheric prog metal and the somber doom of The Gathering. "Loneliness Untold, Loneliness Unfold" features a cinematic intro in the style of an archaic ballad. Organ, acoustic guitar, and raw, anguished vocals define this moment of solitude'cherished by some, feared by many others."Sweet to the Point of Bitter" bursts in, shattering the mood with a barrage from Jonathan's double-kick drum kit and a deluge of tearful, melancholic guitars. Stein's soaring vocals contrast the brutality of the cutting riff against the languid foundation of the infectious chorus."I Am Time" extends the visceral atmosphere, reflecting the doubts inherent in a tragic tale; this is highlighted by orchestration that bridges the 1970s and the new millennium. Bj'rn delivers soothing, majestic, and atmospheric solos; the melody oozes emotion, with a majestic trumpet providing a breath of air'a way to avoid counting the time as it accelerates with advancing age."Fire in Ice" begins with an ambient intro before launching into a frenetic heavy riff driven by thick keyboard tones and double-kick drumming. With its measured vocals, the track plays out as a martial electro-rock ballad, gorging on heavy atmosphere set against soft singing'a classic oxymoron. The song's drift feels oppressive, fanning the embers of this icy air as it snakes into our memory to curl up and stay. The finale machine-guns the air and the ears'a throwback to the sound of yesteryear'before the cinematic feel returns. "Lunar Tale" is as dark as the moon, featuring classical piano and austere vocals'a contemplative ballad about battered memories. Synths amplify the nostalgic aura, leaving one curious about the upcoming album. Ingrid's flute brings serenity, while the outro'evoking an unsettling twilight'sets a signature dreamlike mood: an orgasmic melancholy. "Sanguis (Blood Ties)" is included as a bonus track, ready for a potential radio edit'a nod to the days when such things mattered. And the urge to listen again speaks to the track's spellbinding melody.Green Carnation continues to evolve, offering a more mature, rich sound driven by prominent keyboards. The tracks are dark and somber, with echoes of Emperor and gothic death metal shifting into powerful post-metal and prog-heavy rock'a languid melancholy charged with melodic tension.(4.25)
items._cn_summary: 作为乐队长期沉寂后回归三部曲的第二部，专辑以黑色诗意视角探讨内在旅程与创伤主题。开场曲目将复古管风琴、低音人声与流动重金属 riff 编织成催眠式宏大声景，结合嘶吼唱腔，桥接氛围前卫金属与阴郁厄运摇滚。后续曲目在管风琴、原声吉他与电影化情绪段落之间穿梭，鼓组双踩轰炸配合吉他洪流形成强烈反差，第七十年代管弦配器与新世纪声响交织。钢琴与长笛的片段带来孤寂沉思时刻，合成器放大怀旧氛围，尾声以不安的暮光意象收束。键盘在整体混音中占据突出地位，作品在暗黑沉重基调上融入哥特死亡金属与后金属的碎片，最终呈现出成熟而层次丰富的声响叙事。

items._cn_summary: Burial、Four Tet 与 Thom Yorke 三人合作，从 trip-hop 经典语汇中汲取灵感，推出两首慢节奏作品。整体音效呈现出磁带衰变的质感，模拟老式开盘录音带（reel-to-reel tape）在物理介质上的磨损与失真，营造出一种在怀旧与衰败之间的听觉氛围。这种做旧手法让人联想到 Massive Attack 黄金时期的声音美学，但通过模拟退化介质的方式赋予其新的层次。作品在电子与氛围之间游走，强调的是质感与氛围而非传统歌曲结构，适合偏好沉浸式聆听体验的听众。

items.body:
Thee darkest, weirdest dub perennial from Keith Hudson, 1979, blooms on vinyl for first time in years, ready to scatter smoke and minds into the late and early hours...

First released in 1979 and highly in-demand ever since, the dub sibling to Keith Hudson’s ‘Nuh Skin Up’ pushes that album’s already stark blooz and The Soul Syndicate’s deadly riddims hard into the echo chamber with a balance of experimental nous and heads-down grooves that has assured its place in the pantheon of the most haunting dubs. 

Out of print for decades until a 2007 pressing spiked it back in the water table, the album firmly holds up nearly a half century since its original release on the basis of a future proofed minimalism that continues to haunt successive generations with its bony percussion and a dematerialised soul exemplary of dub metaphysics at its transcendant best.

Up there with the likes of Lee ‘Scratch’ Perry in terms of his dual role as songwriter and desk-tweaking dub maverick, Hudson really gets inside his own tunes, and The Soul Syndicate’s instrumentals, with the uncanniest insight, turning the likes of its title corker into clouds of pillowy steppers bass and streaking echoic contrails.

The way he inverts the vocals on ‘Ire Ire’ to sound properly wrong-end-of-telescope against the foregrounded crack of congas and spectral organ is just magic, and lays the groundwork for so much dub experimentation to come from the likes of everyone from Rhythm & Sound to Tricky, along with the likes of his spellbinding, skeletal steppers dub masterwork ‘Troubles’.
items._genre: dub / experimental dub / roots reggae / dark ambient
items._cn_summary: Keith Hudson 1979年专辑的dub版本，沉寂数十年后重新发行，被乐评视为dub美学的经典之作。制作手法上，制作人深入到自己与The Soul Syndicate的器乐作品中，通过大量回声、混响与声像反转，将原本的blues与riddim推入回声腔室般的空间。评论特别提到《Ire Ire》中人声被反转处理，与前景的conga鼓击和幽灵般的管风琴形成奇异的对立感。整体风格强调极简主义的骨架——骨感的打击乐与去物质化的灵魂感，被比作dub形而上学的典范。乐评将其影响追溯到Rhythm & Sound、Tricky等后世实验者，确立其在dub实验史中的位置。

items.body:
Rolling techno meat motors by one of Amsterdam and Berlin’s trusted, time-honoured producer-DJs.

Dekmantel’s UFO Series of whitelabels hand the reins to DImi Angélis for a grip of cantering, horsepowered hoof taking in the panic-stations drill of ‘GEMx’, a flash of his Dutch techno heritage in the tweaky, Rachmad-esque lead of ‘Hydrophobia’, whilst champing at the bit wit the squiggly bleeps and thundering charge of ‘Sorcery’, and tension between his manic chirrups and robust bassline in ‘Rejuvenator’.
items._cn_summary: Dimi Angélis 为 Dekmantel 旗下白标 UFO Series 推出的 EP《Time Capsule》，延续阿姆斯特丹与柏林 techno 传统的工业化脉络。四首作品以紧凑的节奏推进为骨架：开篇'GEMx'呈现近乎恐慌感的钻击式打击乐密度；'Hydrophobia'以扭动的合成器引线致敬荷兰 techno 经典语汇，Rachmad 式幽暗律动贯穿其中；'Sorcery'用蜿蜒的电子音效与雷鸣般的低频冲击力营造紧张氛围；'Rejuvenator'则在尖锐的信号脉冲与厚重的低音底线之间制造对抗张力。整体制作偏重俱乐部功能性，以马蹄般奔腾的鼓机节奏作为统一美学，呈现成熟稳定的地下 techno 质感，但在声音设计层面未见显著的实验突破。

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. Various Artists - L�ve L�ve (Volume1) (Review) Pedro Lima - Maguidala (Review) Ann O'aro - Bleu (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这是Bongo Joe厂牌发行的圣多美和普林西比70-80年代音乐合辑第二卷，聚焦当地称为Puxa的音乐风格。Puxa融合了非洲葡语国家及加勒比海地区的多种节奏元素，包括merengue、Kompas、Soukouss、Benga等，据说舞蹈时可召灵或驱魔，葡萄牙殖民者曾禁止但未成功。专辑收录15首作品，由Pedro Lima领衔的乐队领衔，多把吉他交织盘旋、主唱与和声相互呼应，节奏层叠绵长，现场演奏常持续数小时。评论指出该音乐虽极具感染力，但由于岛屿面积小、缺乏类似拉各斯或内罗毕的录音产业链，许多音乐未能被记录和发行。整体展现了圣多美独特的音乐创造力与世界音乐融合的丰富可能性。

items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑聚焦贝宁传奇乐队Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与歌手Antoine Dougbé在1977至1982年间的合作录音。Dougbé以拍腿演绎Cavacha节奏而闻名，其作品根植于伏都教传统，并与Congolese流行音乐浪潮紧密相连。乐评指出本辑录音受时代影响，吉他和合成器音色带有八十年代的塑料光泽，但音乐骨架仍扎根于七十年代。与该乐队以往发行相比，本辑的古巴son影响更为明显，尤其在开篇曲目中表现得淋漓尽致。合辑中的歌曲如《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》以合成器铺底，配合闪亮吉他与高帽主导的律动展开层层递进。《We Tayi Sin Assi Tche》则更直接地展现古巴元素，采用经典牛铃与鼻音对唱结构。整体呈现一位风格独特但录音生涯短暂的创作者与一支顶级伴奏乐队之间的化学反应。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合的处女作数字EP，由北欧民谣界经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统素材，乐手各自带来不同视角，整体笼罩着一种古老而略带粗糙的氛围。开场曲粗犷奔腾的节奏为Guldhammer的嗓音提供了展示窗口，唯一的原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus贡献，口琴与风笛推动出强劲律动。传统曲目中，匈牙利扬琴提供了精致的背景，口琴音色与笛子、弦乐交织，制造出不安分且令人兴奋的器乐质感。五首歌展现出乐队超出新人水准的成熟度，作为起点足够扎实，但从评论描述来看仍偏向传统民谣框架内的实验，融合程度有限。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single �A hist�ria de nossa l�ngua� features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including �Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapu�, Ipanema, Maracan�, Capoeira, etc.� This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer�s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track �Ver meu povo se abra�ar� to the convincing reggae of the second single, �Que seja um reggae�. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, �Independ�ncia� features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings �Battre des ailes� accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on �Dans le sud feat�. The gentle �Strati di tempo� is the closest to Santtana�s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz In�cio Lula da Silva�s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political.� For example, on �L�nguas Gerais,� French rapper Oxmo Puccino �speaks about colonization.� Continuing to quote from the liner notes, �Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.� Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing �Cocanha� in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out.� � Like his popular previous recording O Para�so (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Para�so , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message.
